title: Elastic: SANSAR Linux cryptominer fakes GPU readings to hide mining
actor: REF3364 (Elastic's tracking name; financially motivated, unattributed)
summary: Elastic Security Labs describes REF3364, a Linux cryptomining operation seen in late October 2026. Access came through an exposed Ray job agent. The toolkit, SANSAR, adds a kernel rootkit, a modified NVIDIA NVML wrapper that reports 0% GPU use and random temperatures, and an Ethereum-assisted backdoor. Elastic does not identify who is behind it.
plain: Attackers are secretly mining cryptocurrency on Linux servers with powerful graphics cards, and they fake the card's readings so the load looks normal.
exec: Hijacked AI compute raises costs and takes capacity from real workloads, and fake monitoring readings hide it.
action: Do not expose Ray job APIs to the internet, restrict who can submit jobs, and check hosts for a modified NVML library, unknown DKMS modules such as acpi_thermal_mgr and initramfs changes.

key_findings: Organisations running Linux GPU hosts for AI or ML work are the target; three hosts were hit in an intrusion tracked as REF3364 between 22 and 25 October 2026.
Initial access was an internet-reachable Ray job agent that accepted job submissions without authentication, followed by a reverse shell and an added SSH key.
The Rust orchestrator SANSAR takes commands over Tor, runs XMRig and SRBMiner-MULTI for mining, and can open shells and run a TCP SYN flood task.
A kernel rootkit (acpi_thermal_mgr.ko) hides selected processes, files and sockets, and a modified NVML library reports 0% GPU use with random temperature and power readings.
A separate netns backdoor gets its controller address from an Ethereum contract through public RPC and opens a shell on port 8080.
recommendations: Check who can submit jobs to GPU clusters and do not leave job agents such as Ray reachable without authentication.
Check whether GPU monitoring libraries such as NVML have been modified.

validation.note: Elastic's original (Nov 12) read: REF3364, activity Oct 22-25 2026, exposed Ray job agent, NVML wrapper, Turkish comments match; The Hacker News write-up matches.
